title: A coastline that does not stand still
paragraphs: To approach the Korean Peninsula from the sea is to discover that the word coast conceals many landscapes. The eastern shoreline presents long stretches facing deep water and rapid changes in elevation. The western and southern coasts break into bays, tidal channels, sheltered inlets, and islands. No single maritime environment can explain the settlements that developed around the peninsula. A fishing village beside an exposed eastern beach did not confront the same choices as a community living along a western tidal flat.

Sea level also has a history. During colder periods of the distant past, lower global sea levels revealed areas that are submerged today. As climates changed and ice melted, shorelines moved. Archaeological sites now separated from the sea may once have stood near it, while evidence of ancient coastal lives may be hidden below modern waters. This makes the reconstruction of early maritime settlement both fascinating and incomplete. The visible coast is a recent chapter of a much longer geographical story.
